description: Pre-cached high quality MCQs and evaluation explanations for Machine Learning demo fallback

questions.text: Which technique is primarily used to prevent overfitting in deep neural networks by randomly deactivating neuron outputs during training?
What does the Bias-Variance tradeoff represent in supervised machine learning models?
options: The balance between model underfitting (high bias) and overfitting (high variance)
The balance between training speed and GPU memory usage
The choice between classification and regression algorithms
The ratio of training samples to testing samples

questions.text: In binary classification on highly imbalanced datasets, which evaluation metric is preferred over raw accuracy?
Which optimization algorithm updates model parameters iteratively in the direction of the negative gradient of the loss function?
Which machine learning paradigm involves an agent interacting with an environment to maximize cumulative rewards through trial and error?

demo_q1.explanation_correct: Correct! Dropout randomly deactivates neurons during training with a specified probability, forcing the network to learn redundant representations and effectively preventing overfitting.
demo_q1.explanation_incorrect: Incorrect. You selected an incorrect option. Dropout is the technique that randomly zeroes out neuron outputs during training to mitigate overfitting.

demo_q2.explanation_correct: Correct! High bias leads to underfitting simple models, while high variance leads to overfitting noisy training data.
demo_q2.explanation_incorrect: Incorrect. The Bias-Variance tradeoff characterizes the delicate balance between model underfitting (high bias) and overfitting (high variance).

demo_q3.explanation_correct: Correct! F1-score (harmonic mean of precision and recall) and AUC-ROC are robust evaluation metrics for imbalanced classification tasks.
demo_q3.explanation_incorrect: Incorrect. Raw accuracy can be misleading on imbalanced datasets, whereas F1-Score or AUC-ROC accurately measures performance across minority classes.

demo_q4.explanation_correct: Correct! Gradient descent iteratively subtracts the gradient vector of the loss function scaled by learning rate to reach parameter minima.
demo_q4.explanation_incorrect: Incorrect. Gradient Descent optimizes parameters by iteratively stepping opposite to the gradient vector of the loss function.

demo_q5.explanation_correct: Correct! Reinforcement learning formulates problems as Markov Decision Processes where agents receive scalar rewards for selected actions.
demo_q5.explanation_incorrect: Incorrect. Reinforcement learning is based on feedback/reward signals resulting from interaction choices in an environment.
